reviews.title: Dishonest. I signed up for a trial but there is no trial
reviews.text:
I signed up on the premise that I could try this before paying but, after making me a long onboarding questionnaire, they let me see zero content, blocked everything until I pay. 

This is very intentional on their part, and is dishonest.

reviews.title: Meh content. Free trial a hassle to cancel
reviews.text:
I tried this only because of the free trial. Note that your CC will get charged for the full annual premium price immediately. I tried 4-5 of the most interesting ones and quickly learned it wasn’t for me. Trite. Obvious. Maybe I just don’t like self help stuff. 

So when I went to cancel I realized there was no option to cancel. Only to not renew next year. The promised “2 days left” email never came either. Then I became worried I’d been scammed and had no proof there was a free trial. I emailed the company and engaged with a stupidly long back and forth with an AI email bot. I finally got my refund, but it was not smooth and it felt very hidden. They really make you work for it and the AI bot sent a ton of “try this instead” emails first. Hate these kinds of business practices. 

Just listen to podcasts and skip this is my advice.

reviews.title: terrible subscription cancellation method
reviews.text: as the title suggests wonderful  app but when trying to cancel the subscription, it’s almost impossible. I try deleting my account, canceling the subscription in the app. They keep trying to charge me and I’ll try to delete my credit. But it’s not letting me terrible service.

reviews.title: Don’t try it!
reviews.text: Forces you to sign up for a year before you have a chance to evaluate.  Just sent $100 for 1 minute in the app to realize it’s not worth it.  Complete rip off.

reviews.title: Fails

reviews.title: Sneaky subscription practices.
reviews.text:
When you sign up for the seven day free trial, they will tell you that they will email you with two days left to remind you of your upcoming paid subscription. 

What they don’t tell you is they email you every single day (email fatigue) and the message that they send to allow you to opt out of the subscription is titled, “quick one from us.” Vague at best. Easily skipped.  

That email subject slipped through the cracks for me and I was begrudgingly charged for the next year subscription. 

I tried out the service during the first couple of days of my trial and was not impressed

reviews.title: Shady auto renew
reviews.text: Something shady about their auto renew. It didn’t show up as a subscription under my Apple ID like all of my other apps do. So I got billed on auto renew even though I didn’t know I had a subscription.

reviews.title: Feels like a scam.
reviews.text: Signed up for 1 week pro trial to test the app during my commute and see if i would use it. Unfortunately, I was instantly charged full $150 for the annual pricing immediately after subscribing to the 1 week trial. Disappointing and misleading.

reviews.title: Revels in making the complex shallow
reviews.text: I do not know who this app is for . It  is certainly not for people who love reading and love books. Every single book is reduced to how the argument suggested will  can affect one person or the individual rather than the society as a whole. I feel their basic assumption is that people with more money and conservative values are better than others.

reviews.title: Predatory business model, avoid
reviews.text: They don’t just auto subscribe you after the trial. They don’t even just auto subscribe you for a year. They auto subscribe you to a year of their premium subscription for more than $150. Avoid this app at all costs, they’re just predators.

reviews.title: Buyer Beware
reviews.text: I was really intrigued by this app and hoped I would enjoy reading and or listening to their content as much as I enjoy reading and listening to books, but it just didn’t capture my attention.  I had requested to cancel my subscription about 17 days after I purchased it and my request was denied because I contacted them outside the 14 day window. There was no grace period, no compromise to prorate it, nothing.  It is a pretty expensive app “to try” with no option to cancel.  I am very disappointed.

reviews.title: Free trial" charged me $151 immediately
reviews.text:
Start your free 7-day trial" and was charged $151.19 on the spot for a full year of Pro. The subscription didn't appear in my Apple subscriptions because billing goes through Blinkist directly, so it's not easy to find or cancel.

Cancelling took almost an hour: an AI support agent that pushed discounts and upgrades, a "keep my subscription" guilt screen with a video, a survey, and another discount pop-up before the actual cancel option. Support did refund 50% after I complained.

reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.text: Just go with GPT

reviews.title: Automatic yearly charge
reviews.text: Missed the free trial lapse by a day (my fault) but then was charged for a full year, 80 pounds. Tried to dispute it and get it overturned to just paying for a month but was denied. Obviously my fault but I feel that auto charging for a year is bad faith and the first time a company has refused to overturn it in my experience

reviews.title: Onboarding questions lost me before I even use it
reviews.text: I understand the need for personalization, but Blinkist takes it way too far. The initial questionnaire feels like an invasion of privacy and asks deeply personal questions (like sexual satisfaction) that have absolutely zero bearing on my reading preferences. It made me uncomfortable and frustrated before I even started. I wish the app would just let me choose my interests directly instead of trying to psychoanalyze me. I'm sure the content is great, but this initial hurdle killed my motivation to use it.

reviews.title: cannot recommend Blinkist
reviews.text:
First, the library is surprisingly limited! Many popular and key titles I searched for simply aren't available.

Second, the customer support is a complete dead end. Whenever you run into an issue and reach out for help, all you get are canned responses along the lines of "sorry you're running into this problem," with absolutely zero action taken to actually fix or resolve the issue. reviews.title: Caution

reviews.title: Review Replies
reviews.text:
I looked at the app with a view to a subscription. Checked the prices and was OK with them. Then started reading reviews and responses. That’s when I decided against subscribing. 

The stock answer to any review, query, issue, etc is send us a message. They don’t answer questions or respond to issues in the forum. Why?

Responding in the reviews sections surely gives everyone the benefit of the answer, rather than just responding privately to users. The level of repetitive vagueness in the responses stopped me signing up. 

When you charge for your service, you need to do better. I especially expect to see detailed responses to 1 and 2 star reviews. But you can’t be bothered with that. 

Overall, the company’s lack of responses tells me that, customer satisfaction is not a priority. It tells me the company doesn’t care. It tells me they only care about the money, not the product, or the people who buy the product. 

My search continues.

reviews.title: Charged for Premium on a "Basic" account – Refund refused
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with Blinkist’s predatory renewal practices and lack of accountability. I was recently charged for an annual Premium renewal despite the fact that my account dashboard explicitly listed my status as "Basic" (the free tier).
Because the UI showed I was a Basic user, there was no "Cancel Subscription" option available to me. I had no way to stop a renewal that the system claimed didn't exist. I haven't used the app in months and would have canceled long ago if the interface had accurately reflected my status.
When I contacted support, they refused a refund, citing that I am "not a new customer." This is a completely irrelevant excuse. This isn't about a change of heart; it’s about a technical discrepancy on their platform that made it impossible for a user to manage their subscription.
Charging a user while showing them a "Basic" status is misleading at best and a technical bug at worst. Blinkist would rather keep a one-year fee from a non-user than fix a clear error in their system.
Advice to others: Do not trust the account status shown in the app. Check your bank statements and original sign-up emails, because Blinkist’s UI might tell you you’re on the free plan while they’re preparing to charge you for Premium.

reviews.title: Useless, do not buy

reviews.title: Extremely buggy
reviews.text:
I’ve gotten a lot out of the books I’ve listened to so far. However, this experience is ridiculously buggy. Scrolling is very weird/unreliable. I can pause, scroll the text, then resume and it ends up playing from some other completely different part of the book. Also, sometimes a book won’t highlight the text as it’s read. I can’t seem to just start it reading from where I want it to. Would it be so difficult to add a Play option when selecting a word to have it start playing from there? 

This has made for an extremely frustrating experience with the app, almost to the point where I’m going to start looking for alternatives. It’s completely unintuitive how to play, follow along with the text, and hope you don’t do something that will make it start playing somewhere else in the text than you intend.

I’ve also seen chunks of text out of order in a book, coming before where the audio actually starts reading it.

Highlighting is a mess. I’ll select a certain range of text, choose Highlight, and it will move the boundaries of the highlight, leaving off letters at the end and adding more at the beginning. If I tap on a saved highlight, it will open the book but not actually scroll to the highlight. 

You can mark a book as finished, yet it will still show up as In Progress if you have ever gone back and looked at something in it again. Marking it as complete does nothing to resolve this.

It would also be nice to have an option to change the reading voice. It bothers me when som

reviews.title: Capitalism at its finest
reviews.text:
So the app itself I do really enjoy. I love how they summarize books in an easy to read outline that covers all the hot topics so that you can maximize absorption when there’s so much knowledge we want to or feel pressured to take in. Super helpful I especially like the shorts, quick overviews of a range of topics so you can discover new topics and delve deeper if you would like to. I do see an actual benefit for this app HOWEVER, the pricing is absolutely outrageous.
I would have to like take out a loan to be able to pay for this and you can only pay upfront for a year, which is just stupid. I’m sorry. 
When we’re out here taking out loans to fill our tanks they have the audacity to come in and charge $80 for something you might not even use. When I can go to the library read the whole book for free and have access to their free resources
Just another greedy company lining their pockets by duping the American public by overvaluation of their product and knowing that auto charge, they will never return.
Predatory practices at its finest. New apps sometimes avoid this, but they all inevitably go to the dark side.
Sad because it could have been a very fun and useful app

reviews.title: Ai narration is boring
reviews.text: I didn’t realize Blinkist was switching to using AI, otherwise I wouldn’t have gotten a year subscription. I used to be able to stay engaged with Blinkist for hours, but with a monotone robot I have to struggle to pay attention. Probably won’t subscribe next year.

reviews.title: Absolute scam, no refund after cancellation
reviews.text:
I canceled my Blinkist subscription immediately after realizing it wasn’t for me, but they still charged me for the full next year and refused any refund. Customer service gave me the runaround with scripted nonsense about their “policy” while keeping my money.
This is straight-up deceptive billing. I will be reporting Blinkist to every consumer protection agency, the FTC, BBB, my state’s attorney general, and my credit card company for unauthorized charges. If you’re thinking about subscribing, don’t waste your time or money – they make it easy to sign up and nearly impossible to get a fair refund when you cancel.
Stay away!

reviews.title: Lacks many books
reviews.text: Almost every title on my preferred book list was not yet available to listen on the blinklist app so that was very disappointing. Lacking a lot of faith based titles. After listening to many of the “blinks” (15 min book audio clips) available on the app, I don’t feel that I got many good takeaways other than about the millionaire 5 AM morning routine to maximize your daily routine productivity. This was definitely not worth what I paid for the subscription. I’m greatly unsatisfied with the value of this app and would not recommend.

reviews.title: Predatory Practices
reviews.text: They auto-renewed my subscription with zero advance notice. No reminder email or message before charging my card. When I disputed it, their answer delivered by bot was “don’t care.” Reputable services (Netflix, Spotify, NYT) warn you before they bill. Blinkist doesn’t. Turn off auto-renew immediately if you subscribe, or skip it

Now 2026 still not fixed!!! UPDATE FROM FIRST SUBMITTING THIS REVIEW, the response below is clear nobody is listening. Blinkist response, submit a ticket?? I submitted a ticket in 2024 and every year contacted Blinkist to please fix this, and your response is please submit a ticket??

reviews.title: This app used to be good before AI
reviews.text: This app is suffering from AI in two ways. On one hand AI is going to kill its business model because it’s no longer a premium service to get book summaries in audio form. If blinkist used only human reviewers that were not using AI then I’d argue it would still be worth a premium price. But when your “blink” is filled with so many padding words and phrases, a hallmark of AI generated slop, then it defeats the very concept of having short summaries. And that’s the second way AI is killing this service. The quality of the blinks is terrible. Half of everything in the blink is empty text. Reading other reviews it seems like blinkist is in a downward spiral in how they run their business too. Ppl complaining of scammy practices regarding renewals etc. what I observed first hand is they are desperate to get new subs. You can google around and find a link to 80% off of an annual membership. I didn’t use it but the link was live and took me to a page trying to get you to buy now with a fake countdown timer deceiving you with some false scarcity. The other thing I noticed is the moment I cancelled my “free trial” the service stopped working even though I’m entitled to 6 more free days per Apple’s policy. So clearly this is a sinking ship. You’d do better looking for edification elsewhere. It’s sad because when it first started up (a decade ago?) before AI it was actually a really good service that put some effort into generating blinks that were worth reading.

reviews.title: Terrible customer service
reviews.text:
Was charged a full annual subscription without a direct debit, pre notification or even a receipt. Request for a receipt has gone unanswered and contact has been non existent after a kind first acknowledgement. 
Feel cheated and ignored.
